problems.problem: The Step 3 review-sorting rule is much narrower than the search blocks. The focus rule matches only 'fat' or 'muscle', so 7 of the '9 that may bear on your focus' are liver-fat reviews (several in type 2 diabetes). Meanwhile 42011503 ('improvement of body composition') and 42215421 (visceral adipose tissue, with a subgroup without diabetes) were filed under the FACT label 'broader reviews, same drug and people, other outcomes'. The population rule also matched 'with or without diabetes'. Titles truncated at about 80 characters hide the type 2 diabetes populations. The DRAFT did not use the says_type_2_diabetes column that the code had already computed.
problems.cause: The agent wrote the regexes ad hoc in notebook 01_need_A, instead of reusing each block's own term list. Neither the prompt nor the kit requires the title-and-abstract rule to match the search concepts, or treats rule-based groupings as DRAFT.
problems.fix: Kit: add k.sort_reviews(), which builds its focus and population rules from the same block term lists (body composition, lean mass, adipos*, visceral fat, sarcopeni*). It should send 'with or without diabetes' and 'type 2 diabetes' matches to a separate 'mixed or diabetic population' group. Prompt (Step 3): 'Counts per group are FACT; the group labels and what a group means are DRAFT; name the population words each review uses.'

problems.problem: The learning either-or question was asked three times (in 2a, in 2b as part of question 3, and again after an ambiguous 'yes'). Msg 10 itself says 'I am asking about each once'. This created the unscripted turn at msg 15, and the user was irritated. Persona moment 3 required exactly two probes. The When convenient e-mail and model-name request was also repeated at msgs 26 and 30 although never answered.
problems.cause: Prompt 2b says 'ask one either-or question ... never settle an ambiguous yes yourself' without limiting it to one ask per Step 2, and nothing keeps it out of 2a. The rule for 'When convenient' items repeats them in every turn that has no blocking item.
problems.fix: Prompt 2a: 'Ask only the two probes; never the either-or.' Prompt 2b: 'Ask the either-or at most once in Step 2. If it stays unanswered or the reply is an ambiguous yes, put both kinds in the motivation DRAFT marked "to confirm", and let the member strike one on the CERTIFY line.' Prompt or kit: 'Show the When convenient items at set-up and at the pause only.'

problems.problem: Your turn asks Uday to certify 'your purpose line (last reply / two replies ago / three replies back)' but does not show the line again. Self-reports after msgs 25 and 27 say he had to scroll up to see what he was approving.
problems.cause: The prompt has no rule that the reply asking for a certification must show the CERTIFY line itself.
problems.fix: Prompt R-rule on certification: 'Whenever Your turn asks for a certification, show the CERTIFY line (filled in except for the reason) in that same reply, just above Your turn; never refer to an earlier reply.'

problems.problem: The full 12-row plan map appears in 5 of the last 6 replies, together with the glossary and the search cards. Self-reports for msgs 13, 21, 23 and 29 complain about length, and the user did not take in the search strings that had been shown. Prose metrics pass only because tables are excluded.
problems.cause: The prompt's map rule fires at each certification, step change, request and pause, even when these come in consecutive turns, and offers no compact form.
problems.fix: Prompt: 'Show the full map at most once every 3 replies (always on request and at the pause). Otherwise show k.steps_line(): one line with the changed rows only.' Kit: steps_line() should list only the steps whose status changed.

problems.problem: The log records Uday as having accepted the full composed purpose statement (L000040, at msg 13) and the full Individual Motivation line (L000058, at msg 15) before either wording had been shown. Msg 20 then says 'your purpose, as you accepted it'. Msg 16 asks him to 'check your draft purpose statement', which had only appeared as a table row; the self-report after msg 17 says 'no purpose statement has been shown yet'.
problems.cause: The kit's propose/accept flow logs acceptance of a composed text, and prompt 2b treats the confirmed reflection as the proposed purpose statement without first showing it in its final form.
problems.fix: Prompt 2b: 'Show the composed purpose statement in the reflection reply so that "yes" accepts that exact text.' Kit: when accepts_draft is inferred from a reflection, log 'accepted the reflection (components)', and word msg 20 as 'built from the reflection you confirmed'.

problems.problem: The OpenAlex Search 3 card has no per-block counts. Its purpose is given only as 'reviews', and its block explanation sits in the DRAFT table, not on the card. Its fat-or-muscle block also drops terms the PubMed block uses (adipos*, visceral fat, body fat, sarcopeni*) without saying so. This is why M4 scored 1.
problems.cause: The kit's openalex_works and search_report produce no block-count card for OpenAlex. The prompt does not require the same blocks, or a note of differences, across sources.
problems.fix: Kit: run each OpenAlex block with per-page=1 to read meta.count, and render the same block table used for PubMed. Prompt: 'Each source's card states its purpose in the team's words and lists any terms that differ from the PubMed blocks.'

problems.problem: Technical terms are unexplained at first use. 'PubMed, OpenAlex, ClinicalTrials.gov' appear in the set-up line at msg 14, but the glossary only arrives at msg 22, and ClinicalTrials.gov is never explained. 'Latest search end' (msg 22) is not explained either. This is why M6 scored 1.
problems.cause: The md from kit setup() names the sources without glosses, and the glossary is tied to the first search card.
problems.fix: Kit setup() md: 'Search tools work: PubMed (medical journal index), OpenAlex (open index of research papers), ClinicalTrials.gov (registry of clinical trials).' Prompt glossary: add 'search end (the last date a review searched the literature)'.

problems.problem: 'Searches run this session: 12' counts the OpenAlex ('systematic review') and ClinicalTrials.gov ('asthma') smoke tests as searches. Those two are also logged with element LU and no 'smoke test' purpose. Separately, plan.yaml's LU query list omits the real OpenAlex search L000080.
problems.cause: The kit's smoke_test() calls openalex_works and ctgov_studies with element='LU' and no purpose, and session_summary filters out only the PubMed smoke tests.
problems.fix: Kit: tag every smoke-test call with purpose='smoke test' and element=None, exclude them in session_summary, and add every query to the element it served (here NR) in plan.yaml.

problems.problem: The helper kit stopped with an error while showing a search, because team.yaml stored sources as the text 'not given' (set for solo planners). The agent had to rewrite the team entry and reset a 'shown' key in the session state (correction L000072), which risks edits that bypass the kit.
problems.cause: Kit bug: set_team records skipped solo items as strings, while search_report expects a list.
problems.fix: Kit: store skipped team items as [] with a not_given flag, check the types in set_team, and never mark a search key as shown until its md has been returned.

problems.problem: Uday never consented to his exact words being kept, so summaries were the default. Yet the certification records keep his exact messages ('said': 'testing the workflow', 'certify, focus is right'), the chat shows his reasons verbatim in the CERTIFY lines, and L000002 quotes 'passed 16/16. begin'.
problems.cause: Prompt 2.1 says 'never quote their words, even one', while 3.10 requires said=<the reviewer's message> and reason=<their reason as given>. k.init stores the begin message as given.
problems.fix: Prompt 2.1: 'Certification messages and reasons are always recorded as given; say so when asking for consent. Everything else follows the member's consent choice.' Kit: init(calibration=) should record only the score and the critical-question result.

judge.strengths: Certification was handled with integrity. A bare 'Certify' was turned down with a single reason question, the agent never suggested a reason, the wording certified matched the wording shown, and the status line was always accurate. The focus came from Uday's own words: probes turned 'all of it' into 'whether the weight lost is fat or muscle', the narrowing was reconciled (msg 12, 'Added by me: nothing'), and the focus was then carried into the purpose line and the search labels. The early start of Step 3 was announced and flagged, with the purpose kept open, and the pending certification was asked for again each turn. Searches were shown openly: PubMed strings with per-block counts, Create Date bounds, Sources lines with log ids, the 100-of-12,193 limit for OpenAlex, and the sources not yet searched. Every number was produced by the kit or notebook code from saved raw files. The records agree with each other (log, plan.yaml, team.yaml, git commits, summary). The agent was honest about what was unknown (search-end dates, full texts not read). Nothing had to be read in a file: the files opened beside the chat were extras, and the records were packaged only at the pause.
